Welcome to the support page for Earshot — Voice to Text. If you experience any issues, have questions, or want to provide feedback, please contact us using the information below.

Email: vincenttrandeveloper@gmail.com You can also send a bug report, feedback, or a feature suggestion directly from the app — open Settings → Feedback. Reports sent this way include your app version, which helps us diagnose issues faster. We aim to respond as quickly as possible.

Earshot transcribes your recordings and identifies speakers entirely on your iPhone — nothing is sent to a server. If results seem off: Background noise, overlapping speech, and distance from the microphone all affect accuracy — try recording closer to the speakers in a quieter space. Speaker identification is a best-effort suggestion, not a certified match — you can rename or correct a speaker label at any time. Make sure the Microphone and Speech Recognition permissions are granted — Settings → Earshot. For longer or more accurate transcripts, try enabling the on-device AI model in Settings.

The improved on-device AI option downloads one model file so summaries and answers can be generated without a network connection. This requires an internet connection only for the initial download — after that, it runs fully offline. If the download fails or stalls, check your connection and available storage, then try again from Settings. Switching this off does not delete your existing transcripts or summaries.

Earshot offers optional paid plans (monthly, yearly, and lifetime). Purchases are managed entirely through Apple and the App Store. To restore a purchase on a new device or after reinstalling, open Settings → Restore Purchases while signed in to the same Apple Account used for the original purchase. For billing issues, cancellations, or refunds, use Apple's own subscription management: iOS: Settings → [Your Name] → Subscriptions

Earshot stores your recordings, transcripts, and speaker data only on your device — there is no cloud sync by default and we hold no copy. Deleting the app or clearing its data removes everything permanently, and we cannot restore it for you. If you want a copy kept somewhere else, use the in-app export feature, or turn on the optional iCloud backup (Pro) in Settings, which writes a copy into your own iCloud account.

Before contacting support, please try: Restarting the app Updating to the latest app version Restarting your device Reinstalling the app if necessary — note that this erases your local recordings and transcripts unless you have exported them or enabled iCloud backup

Effective date: September 16, 2026 Last updated: September 16, 2026 Publisher / data controller: WBB Contact: vincenttrandeveloper@gmail.com

Earshot is built so that what you record stays yours. Your recordings and transcripts never leave your device. Speech-to-text, speaker identification, AI summaries, and search all run on your iPhone. There is no server that receives your audio, your transcripts, or anything derived from them (speaker labels, voice embeddings, summaries, search index). There is no account. No sign-up, no email required, no password, no social login. Nothing ties the app to your identity. No ads, no ad SDKs, no tracking across other apps or websites. Earshot does not use the advertising identifier (IDFA) and does not show the App Tracking Transparency prompt, because it has nothing to track you with. We never sell your personal information. What does leave the device: anonymous usage statistics and crash reports (to make the app work better), device-attestation tokens (to stop abuse of our servers), anonymous purchase/entitlement events (to unlock what you bought), and — only if you choose to use them — the content of a report you submit through the in-app feedback form, an optional AI model file you choose to download, or an optional iCloud backup you turn on yourself. The rest of this policy explains each of those points precisely.

This policy applies to the Earshot app distributed on the Apple App Store, and to any future updates, to the extent that the features described are actually enabled on your device. Earshot is iOS-only; there is no Android or Google Play version of this policy to reconcile. It does not cover Apple's own processing of your data as the platform and store operator — including iCloud, if you choose to use the optional backup feature described in section 3.8 — which is governed by Apple's own privacy policy.

Earshot stores the following locally on your phone only. None of it is transmitted to us, and none of it is transmitted to any third party as part of normal use of the app. What Details Audio recordings The .m4a audio file of each recording you make. Transcripts The text Earshot recognizes from your recording, word timestamps, and your own edits (with the original wording kept alongside your edit so you can compare or undo). Speaker data Which parts of a recording were spoken by which speaker, a voice embedding used to recognize the same speaker again in a later recording (Pro), and any name you give a speaker. Summaries, titles, and checklists AI-generated summaries, an AI-generated title, and a checklist of follow-ups Earshot extracts from a recording. Search index A numeric representation (embedding) of each transcript segment, used so you can search your library by meaning as well as by keyword (Pro). Tags and bookmarks Any tag you create and assign to a recording, and any moment in a transcript you bookmark (Pro). An optional AI model file If you choose to enable the improved on-device AI option (Pro), Earshot downloads one AI model file and stores it on your device so summaries and answers can be generated locally without a network connection. See section 3.6. Preferences Language, appearance, which AI engine you've chosen, whether Face ID lock is on, and other app settings. Purchase entitlement state A local record of whether a paid plan is active, so the app knows what to unlock while offline. An anonymous ID for the feedback form A randomly generated identifier (a UUID), created only if you open the feedback form. It is not derived from your device, phone number, email, or advertising identifier. It exists so that if you send several reports we can see they came from the same install. Your email, if you typed one into the feedback form Remembered locally so you do not have to retype it next time. Deletion. All of the above is removed when you delete a recording in the app, delete the app, or clear the app's data in your device settings. Because we never receive it, we cannot restore it for you — use the export or iCloud backup features described below if you want a copy kept somewhere else.
documents.s: 2. Data that stays on your device

documents.t: Earshot records anonymous, aggregated usage events so we can see which features are used and where people get stuck. Examples of what is recorded: which screen you are viewing (Record, Library, Session Detail, Settings, Feedback, Paywall); that a recording started, finished, or failed, and roughly how long it ran — never its content; that speaker identification, a summary, or a search ran, and which engine produced it (the built-in free method, or the optional on-device AI model) — never the transcript, the summary text, the speaker names, or the search query itself; that the paywall was opened, a plan was selected, and whether a purchase started, completed, failed, or was cancelled — and which plan tier, never payment details; that "restore purchases" was tapped; that the app's rating prompt was shown; that a feedback report was submitted, and how many images were attached. What is never sent as analytics: the audio itself, the text of your transcripts, summaries, speaker names, tags, or search queries. Event values are limited in length and stripped to plain identifiers before being sent. Firebase assigns an app-instance ID to your installation and receives basic technical context (platform, OS version, app version, device model, coarse region/language, IP address at the time of the request). Earshot is configured without advertising-identifier support, so no IDFA is collected and this data is not used for advertising or cross-app tracking. The app-instance ID is reset if you delete and reinstall the app, or clear app data. Processor: Google LLC / Firebase — see the Firebase privacy documentation.

If the app crashes or hits a fatal error, a crash report is sent so we can fix it. A report contains the stack trace, the app version, the device model, the OS version, and technical state at the moment of the crash. It does not contain your recordings, transcripts, or any of their content, and it is not used to identify you. Processor: Google LLC / Firebase.

Before Earshot talks to our Firebase services, it asks the operating system to prove the app is a genuine, untampered install (App Attest / DeviceCheck). The result is a short-lived attestation token. This protects our backend from spam and abuse. The token attests the app, not you — it carries no personal data and cannot be used to identify you. Processor: Apple Inc. (App Attest / DeviceCheck) and Google LLC (Firebase App Check).
documents.s: 3.3 Abuse prevention — Google Firebase App Check

documents.t: Earshot reads a small, public, read-only configuration document from Cloud Firestore at startup, gated by App Check with no sign-in of any kind. It tells the app things like whether the feedback form is currently accepting submissions, and which on-device AI model options are currently offered. This is a read only — nothing about you is sent. As with any network request, Google receives your IP address and basic technical data to serve the response.

This is the only place in normal use where you deliberately send us content. It is entirely optional — the app is fully usable without ever opening it. When you submit a report, the following is stored in Cloud Firestore and Firebase Storage: the email address you enter (so we can reply — you choose whether to give a real one); the report type (bug report, feedback, or feature suggestion); your message (up to 2,000 characters); up to 3 images you attach (max 5 MB each); the anonymous ID described in section 2, the app version, and a server timestamp. Your recordings and transcripts are never attached automatically. If you choose to describe a problem by attaching a screenshot, only the image you explicitly pick is uploaded — the photo picker never gives Earshot access to your photo library as a whole, and Earshot does not read location or other metadata from the images you attach. Retention. Reports are kept while we work through them and for a reasonable period afterwards as a record of what was fixed and why. You can ask us to delete your report and its attachments at any time — see section 9.
documents.s: 3.5 The in-app feedback form (bug report / feedback / feature suggestion)

documents.t: If you turn on the improved on-device AI option in Settings, Earshot downloads one AI model file over HTTPS from a third-party file-hosting service, Hugging Face, and stores it on your device. This is a plain file download: your device's IP address and standard request metadata reach Hugging Face's servers, exactly as with any file download from any website, but no recording, transcript, or other content of yours is sent as part of this download — the traffic only pulls a generic, publicly published model file, it never uploads anything. Once downloaded, the model runs entirely on your device; nothing about how you use it is sent anywhere. Processor: Hugging Face, Inc. — file delivery only, no personal data exchanged.

Earshot offers optional paid plans (monthly, yearly, and a one-time lifetime purchase). Payment itself is processed entirely by Apple through the App Store on your device. We never see or receive your card number, bank details, or billing address. Earshot uses RevenueCat to determine which plan is active and unlock the right features. RevenueCat receives an anonymous, RevenueCat-generated identifier for your install (Earshot does not log this identifier in with any account, because there is no account), which App Store product you purchased, whether it is active, and basic device/platform information. This entitlement state is also cached locally so the app knows what to unlock while offline. "Restore purchases" asks Apple and RevenueCat to re-report purchases already tied to your Apple Account. Managing or cancelling a subscription opens Apple's own subscription management screen. Processors: RevenueCat, Inc. (entitlement management) and Apple Inc. (App Store billing). Apple's handling of your purchase data is governed by Apple's privacy policy, not this one; RevenueCat's is governed by RevenueCat's privacy policy.
documents.s: 3.7 Purchases and subscriptions — RevenueCat and Apple

documents.t: If you turn on iCloud backup in Settings, Earshot writes a copy of your session library — transcripts, speaker data, and the audio files — into a private container inside your own iCloud account, so a lost or new phone does not mean a lost library. This is: off by default — nothing is backed up unless you turn it on; one-way, restore-on-demand — Earshot writes files there and can read them back to restore a library, but this is not a live, continuous, multi-device sync; stored under your Apple ID's iCloud storage, not on a server we operate. We never receive a copy of it. Apple's handling of the data in your iCloud account is governed by Apple's own privacy policy, and it counts against your iCloud storage quota.

Earshot does not send push notifications and has no push infrastructure — it registers no push token and cannot message you from our side. While recording, the app can show a Live Activity (Lock Screen / Dynamic Island) with the current recording duration (Pro); this is drawn locally by the app on your device and involves no server or notification service.

Earshot may ask the operating system to display the native App Store rating dialog. The dialog, and any review you write in it, are handled by Apple. We only record internally that the prompt was shown (see section 3.1); we never see whether or how you rated the app.

Permission Why Required? Microphone To record the audio you choose to capture. Recordings never leave your device. Required to record Speech Recognition To transcribe your recordings to text entirely on your device. Nothing is sent to a server as part of this. Required to transcribe Face ID To lock the app, or a single recording (Pro), so only you can open it. Face ID matching happens entirely within the operating system; Earshot never sees or stores your biometric data. Optional Photo library (selected photos only) To attach an image to a feedback report you are sending us. The system photo picker is used, so Earshot never gets access to your photo library as a whole. Optional Earshot deliberately does not request or use: camera, contacts, location, calendar, reminders, health data, motion sensors, or the advertising identifier / App Tracking Transparency prompt.
documents.s: 4. Permissions Earshot asks for — and the ones it does not

documents.t: We process the limited data described above to: provide recording, transcription, speaker identification, summaries, search, and export; keep the app stable — diagnosing crashes and errors; understand which features are used, so we know what to improve; unlock paid features you bought, via Apple and RevenueCat; reply to a feedback report you sent us, and fix what it describes; protect our services from abuse and comply with legal obligations. We do not use your data for advertising, profiling, automated decision-making, or cross-app or cross-site tracking. We do not sell personal information, and we do not "share" it for cross-context behavioural advertising as those terms are used in California law.

Where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies to you: Purpose Legal basis Providing the app's features Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)) Crash reporting, abuse prevention, security Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)) — keeping the app working and our services safe Usage analytics Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)), or your consent where local law requires it Handling a feedback report you send us Performance of a contract / your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) — you choose to send it Purchases and entitlement Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)) Optional AI model download / iCloud backup Your consent — you turn each on yourself (Art. 6(1)(a)) Legal and record-keeping obligations Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)) You may object to processing based on legitimate interests, and withdraw consent at any time — for the optional features above, by turning them off in Settings.

Recipient Role Data involved Google LLC / Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics, App Check, Firestore, Storage, Remote Config Usage events, crash reports, attestation tokens, feedback content, IP address RevenueCat, Inc. Purchase/entitlement management Anonymous purchaser ID, product ID, purchase status, device/platform info Apple Inc. App Store distribution, in-app purchases, App Attest, optional iCloud backup, Face ID, rating prompt Purchase and entitlement data, attestation, iCloud-stored backup (under your own Apple ID) Hugging Face, Inc. Delivery of an optional, publicly published AI model file IP address and standard request metadata only — no personal content These providers process data on servers in the United States and other countries, which may be outside your country of residence. Where required, such transfers rely on the safeguards those providers offer — including the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses and, where applicable, the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Each provider processes data under its own privacy policy. We use no advertising networks, no attribution or MMP SDKs, and no analytics providers beyond the ones named above.

Data Kept for Everything in section 2 (on your device) Until you delete it in the app, clear app data, or uninstall Earshot Analytics events For the retention period configured in Firebase Analytics (by default up to 14 months for event-level data), then deleted or aggregated Crash reports Typically up to 90 days, per Crashlytics' retention Feedback reports and attached images While being handled, and for a reasonable period afterwards as a record; deleted earlier on request Purchase/entitlement data at RevenueCat For as long as needed to provide entitlement service, per RevenueCat's own retention policy iCloud backup (if enabled) Until you turn the feature off, delete the backup, or delete your iCloud data — controlled entirely by you App Check tokens Short-lived; refreshed automatically and not retained as records

Depending on where you live — including under the GDPR/UK GDPR, the CCPA/CPRA in California, and comparable laws elsewhere — you may have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict, or object to the processing of your personal information, to receive a copy of it in a portable format, to withdraw consent, and not to be discriminated against for exercising these rights. In practice, for Earshot: Data on your device — you control it directly. Delete individual recordings in the app, clear the app's data in system settings, or uninstall the app. We hold no copy, so there is nothing for us to delete. Analytics and crash data — reinstalling the app, or clearing app data, resets the app-instance ID and disconnects future data from past data. To have data associated with your current installation deleted, email us; we will need the approximate dates so we can locate it. Purchase/entitlement data at RevenueCat — email us and we will submit a deletion request on your behalf, or contact RevenueCat directly. A feedback report you sent us — email us from the address you used, or quote the report, and we will delete the report and its attachments. iCloud backup — delete it yourself from Settings, or from your iCloud storage settings; we never hold a copy. Write to vincenttrandeveloper@gmail.com. We aim to respond within 30 days. You may also lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority; in the EEA, that is the authority for your country of residence.

Earshot is a general-audience utility app. It is not directed at children under 13 (or the higher minimum age set by your local law, such as 16 in parts of the EEA), and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children. The app contains no ads, no social features, no user-to-user content, and no external links other than to the App Store. If you are a parent or guardian and believe a child has sent us personal information through the feedback form, contact us and we will delete it.

Earshot lets you record audio you capture with your device's microphone, including conversations with other people. You are responsible for complying with the law that applies to you — including any requirement to obtain the other participants' consent before recording a conversation, which varies by country, and in the United States, by state. We do not monitor, moderate, or have access to what you record, and we cannot advise you on the recording-consent law in your specific situation.

Data on your device is protected by the operating system's app sandbox and device encryption. Data in transit is sent over HTTPS/TLS. Access to our Firebase project is restricted to the publisher, requests are attested with App Check, and Firestore security rules limit what the app can read and write. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

We may update this policy as the app changes. The "Last updated" date at the top will change, and for material changes — for example a genuinely new category of data collection — we will give notice in the app or on the store listing before the change takes effect. Continuing to use the app after a change takes effect means the updated policy applies.

By downloading, installing, accessing, or using the Earshot application (the "App"), you acknowledge that you have read, understood, and agree to be bound by these Terms of Use. If you do not agree, do not use the App.

The App records audio you choose to capture and transcribes it to text, identifies different speakers in a recording (Pro), generates AI summaries, titles, and checklists, lets you search your recordings, and lets you export transcripts in several formats. Recording, transcription, speaker identification, and AI features run entirely on your device; see the Privacy Policy for exactly what does and does not leave your device. We may add, change, or suspend features without advance notice where permitted by law. The App is provided "as is." We do not warrant that the App will be uninterrupted, error-free, or suitable for every device or your specific purpose. In particular: Transcription, speaker identification, summaries, and any other AI-generated output may be inaccurate, incomplete, or misattributed. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying anything the App produces before relying on it — for example before using it as a record of what was said, for a legal, medical, academic, or business purpose, or for any decision with real consequences. Speaker identification is a best-effort estimate. Where the App suggests that a voice matches someone identified in an earlier recording, this is a suggestion for you to confirm, not a certified identification of a person.

The App lets you record audio using your device's microphone, including conversations with other people. You are solely responsible for complying with the law that applies to you when you make a recording — including any requirement to inform or obtain the consent of the other people being recorded, which varies by country and, in the United States, by state (some require the consent of only one party to the conversation; others require the consent of everyone on the recording). You must not use the App to record anyone unlawfully, or in violation of a duty of confidentiality you owe them. We take no position on, and give no advice about, whether any particular recording you intend to make is lawful in your situation. If in doubt, ask a lawyer before recording, not us.
Use of the App does not require you to create an account with us. If the App later offers sign-in or server sync, any additional terms will be disclosed in the App or added to this document.

Paid plans are billed through the Apple App Store, subject to Apple's own terms and policies. The App uses RevenueCat to manage which plan is active on your device; see the Privacy Policy for what RevenueCat receives.

Earshot Pro is offered as: a monthly auto-renewing subscription; a yearly auto-renewing subscription; and a one-time lifetime purchase (not a subscription — pay once, keep Pro for as long as you use the App). The exact price, any free trial, and what each plan currently unlocks are shown on the in-app purchase screen before you buy, and may change over time — the terms shown to you at the moment of purchase govern that purchase.

Monthly and yearly plans are automatically renewing unless described otherwise at purchase. Manage or cancel a subscription in Settings → [Your Name] → Subscriptions on your device, per Apple's instructions. To avoid being charged for the next period, cancel at least 24 hours before the current period ends. The lifetime plan is a one-time purchase — there is nothing to cancel or renew.
Displayed prices may include or exclude taxes and fees depending on your region and Apple's policies. The amount charged is confirmed on the App Store's payment screen.
Refund, return, or billing disputes for transactions on the App Store are handled under Apple's policies, not directly by us, except where mandatory law provides otherwise.

Recordings, transcripts, and everything else described in the Privacy Policy's section 2 stay on your device regardless of your plan — cancelling Pro does not delete anything you have already recorded or transcribed. It does mean that Pro-only features (speaker ID, semantic search, extra export formats, bookmarks, per-recording lock, iCloud backup, Live Activity) stop working going forward, and that an on-device AI model you had downloaded may no longer be selectable until you resubscribe or repurchase.
